I wrote `debts.txt` with all 30 negative balances, but 22 of them are not exact copies. In `units.md`, balances of 1,000 or more use a non-breaking space between the thousands and the rest of the number, as in `−1 432,71`. My file has a normal space there, because the Write and Edit tools saved my non-breaking space as a normal one. A second try with Edit didn't fix it.

Everything else matches the source. The lines are in table order, with the code, a tab, then the balance. The codes keep their mixed alphabets: 5 codes are in Latin letters (`KE-4052`, `MT-5107`, `EH-9389`, `AA-0905`, `TM-1898`) and the other 25 are in Cyrillic. The minus sign is the same `−` character as in the source, not a hyphen. I checked all of this with Grep searches on both files, without running any code.

Do you want me to fix the 22 spaces with one `sed` command? That would break your "no shell commands" rule, so I won't run it unless you say yes.
